deploy-bot: deploycheck: release rc-2026.03.10 - vuln-scan: 1 LOW severity transitive lib 'libfasttext' (CVE-2025-XXXX). SBOM attached -> s3://redwood-artifacts/rc-2026.03.10/sbom.json

maya: heads up — EU canary starts in 30m, change window ends 18:00 PT. do we want to pause EU?

liam: low sev and transitive, likely false positive for runtime exploitability. but eu canary policy is strict. my vote: regional carveout for EU + continue global rollout.

olga: agree with carveout. operationally: we need clear rollback criteria and release-notes wording. if we pause EU, make sure trace hooks and alerts are enabled.

zoe: product prefers no global delay. can you scope the carveout so only the EU canary is paused? i'll craft customer-facing note if no global impact.

liam: we can apply a short exemption with deploybot, timebox it. example command: `deploybot exempt --region=eu --policy=sbom-scan --duration=4h --reason "transitive low sev"`

maya: sounds good. @liam please file the exemption ticket and add a line to the release notes draft. @olga can you confirm exact rollback triggers?

olga: rollback triggers: (1) new SCA flag at >=MED, (2) exploitability score change, (3) canary error rate >0.5% for 10m. i'll add these to the runbook and enable tracing.

deploy-bot: exemption ticket created -> EX-4921. Action: EU canary paused, non-EU canaries continuing. Exemption expires in 4h unless extended. SBOM and scan report attached to ticket.

liam: :thumbsup: updating release notes: "EU rollout paused pending SBOM provenance verification; global availability unchanged."

zoe: i'll draft a short customer note and engineering blurb for release notes. sending in ~15m.

maya: LGTM. timebox 4h then reassess. @olga please monitor traces and escalate if triggers hit. thanks team :rocket:
